sources.title: Immigration (Visa) Order: Revised Laws current record
sources.officialityEvidence: The Attorney General Chambers’ live Revised Laws 2023 record identifies the Immigration (Visa) Order and its 2020 amendment as in force, with its current numbered schedules.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Amended by S.I. 134/2020 .. in force 7 September 2020.

sources.title: Immigration (Visa) Order, Schedule 1
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Revised Laws Schedule 1 names several scoped countries as visa-required, but does not by itself settle their actual issuance timing against the current airport service or the other schedules.
sources.supportingExcerpt: COUNTRIES WHOSE SUBJECTS OR CITIZENS REQUIRE A VISA TO ENTER SAINT LUCIA

sources.title: Immigration (Visa) Order, Schedule 2
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Revised Laws Schedule 2 is the current statutory list for nationalities that may be issued a visa on arrival. It names Georgia and the legacy term Zaire, creating material issues for the scoped Georgia and DR Congo rows.
sources.supportingExcerpt: COUNTRIES WHOSE SUBJECTS OR CITIZENS MAY BE ISSUED A VISA ON ARRIVAL IN SAINT LUCIA

sources.title: Apply for Saint Lucia Non-Immigrant Visa
sources.publisher: Ministry of External Affairs, International Trade, Civil Aviation and Diaspora Affairs
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Ministry service says only some foreign nationals need a visa, directs application at least two weeks before travel, and describes airport filing as case-specific and potentially refused rather than a nationality-wide arrival route.
sources.supportingExcerpt: In some circustances, application for a visa can be made at the airport on entry to Saint Lucia

sources.title: Saint Lucia and Georgia conclude visa waiver agreement
sources.publisher: Ministry of External Affairs, Saint Lucia
sources.officialityEvidence: The current official 2022 announcement records signature and intended visa-free travel, but publishes no entry-into-force date or current-force confirmation.
sources.supportingExcerpt: The agreement will facilitate the travel of nationals of the two countries to each other’s territory without a visa
